src.label: Embassy of Kenya in Spain — Ministry of Livestock Development conditions for importing dogs and cats

head: Kenya wants an import permit, a rabies-tested animal and cargo shipment, not cabin travel.
lines: The Kenyan ministry conditions (published by the embassy in Spain) say a dog or cat needs an international veterinary certificate dated no more than 48 hours before embarkation, showing no sign of rabies or other contagious disease and no internal or external parasites.

Unless the animal spent its first six months in a rabies-free country, it needs a permanent mark such as a microchip, a rabies vaccine given 6 to 12 months before shipment (primary dose from 3 months of age) or within a year (booster), and a rabies antibody test of at least 0.5 IU/ml taken 3 to 24 months before shipment. Animals that do not meet this may be quarantined for up to six months at the owner's cost.

The import permit is valid for a maximum of 30 days and for one consignment, and must travel with the animal. The airline captain must certify the animal stayed on the aircraft and apart from other dogs and cats. The ministry text states that animals travel as manifest cargo in the freight hold, not as baggage or in the cabin.
